speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Prime Minister what are the measures that MAS takes to ensure that the automated teller machines (ATMs) of local banks are fully interoperable to enable cash withdrawals and bank transactions to be more accessible to the elderly and those with mobility needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: First, let me say that we have seen a very significant increase in the number of automated teller machines (ATMs) over the last decade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Taken as a percentage of the resident population, the number increased by 47%, a very significant increase over 10 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If I compare this, for instance, to Hong Kong, which is the closest to us as a densely populated city-state, the coverage of ATMs in Singapore is about 38% greater on a geographical basis, in other words, per kilometer (km), and also significantly higher on a per capita basis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This coverage that I have mentioned is based on households' access to two local bank networks, that is, the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS)/Post Office Savings Bank network on one hand, and the United Overseas Bank/Overseas Chinese Banking Corporation network on the other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: But each of these two ATM networks has a high coverage in their own right.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In other words, each of them has at least 90% of HDB households having access to their ATM networks within 500 metres of their homes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Furthermore, I should say that ATMs and bank branches are not the only ways in which people get convenient access to cash, and access to cash is, in fact, the main usage of ATMs today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Cash-back services at retail outlets enable customers to make cash withdrawals from their bank accounts when they make purchases at these outlets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For example, the three local banks have partnered 7-Eleven stores to provide cash-back services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: That is quite convenient because they are in most neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: DBS has also partnered eight other large retailers, such as Giant, Sheng Siong, Cold Storage and SingPost outlets to provide cash-back services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These are bank branches, ATMs and non-bank cash withdrawal points, taken together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Nevertheless, we continue to monitor the accessibility of basic banking services in Singapore for different segments of the population.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We know that the older population will become increasingly important.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We also continue to work with the banks to promote awareness of the various other touchpoints besides the banks and ATMs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam) (for the Prime Minister)
text: And we continue to promote, particularly for the younger and middle-aged population, the use of digital payments and other digital basic banking services.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I was wondering if the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) might want to explore different ways of measuring the distance to the nearest ATM, if MAS is not already doing so.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: For example, distance according to "the crow flies" versus distance traversed on the ground by able-bodied pedestrians or, for that matter, barrier-free distance on the ground.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: These various metrics may be useful to understand how different segments of the population will be affected, especially as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: The figures I mentioned are based on distances by how "the crow flies".

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: I am not sure if this is wild crows or domestic crows, but I can check on that and let the Member know.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: It does make sense to look at walking distances and, in fact, we are using third-party software to try and estimate how long it takes and how far it is on walking routes in the various neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: There are also, for instance, issues of queues if you were to make everything completely interoperable.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: But we are not foreclosing the issue from MAS' point of view.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: I just want to repeat the point that currently, each of the two local banks' ATM networks has a very high degree of coverage.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: They are competing with each other in the same neighbourhoods, but each of them has got at least 90% of HDB households having access to their ATMs within 500 metres of their homes.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: But it is something which we would continue to look at.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Since there is already 90% coverage, for the remaining 10%, will the Ministry be working with the banks to ensure this 10% will be taken care of as well?

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: My sentiments are in line with Members on this.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: We do want to have adequate coverage of basic banking services.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: We have to break that down into cash withdrawals, cash deposits, transfer of funds and different services which are used by different segments of the population.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: It does cost something and it is not the only solution.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: We should maximise availability of other cash withdrawal touchpoints across the island.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: I am glad that the banks are doing this, not just with 7-Eleven stores but other stores, in a way that is convenient to residents.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: So, let us take a holistic view, maximise access for the normal, basic transactions people need to make and be mindful of the older population because we do not want them to walk too far when they have to make a transaction.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: But it is not just a matter of ATM networks.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: I am not saying that that is the only benchmark.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: We do want to improve the availability of basic banking services around the island.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: We will look at the ATM network to see whether access can be further improved, but it is not the only solution.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It seems to me that with our mobile penetration being very high at 150%, and with eight million mobile phones within our small city-state, clearly, that should be the strategy.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: If so, why would ATMs matter so much in the future?

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: I am glad Mr Cedric Foo has raised this point and it is something which I referred to earlier.

speaker: Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam
text: That is the key strategy; and the Member has put it very well.
